title: Ultraviolet radiation — fact sheet
claims: Globally in 2020, over 1.5 million cases of skin cancers were diagnosed and over 120,000 skin cancer-associated deaths were reported.
Sun protection is recommended when the UV Index is 3 or above.
Wraparound-style sunglasses providing 99–100% UV-A and UV-B protection are recommended.
Sunscreens should not be used to extend time spent in the sun; sun protection is best achieved by seeking shade and wearing clothes.
Worldwide, an estimated 15 million people are blind due to cataracts, and about 10% of these may be due to UV exposure.
Small amounts of UV are essential for vitamin D production, but excessive exposure is carcinogenic to humans.
People taking photosensitising medication and those with a family history of skin cancer are at increased risk.
